# Quickstart: Authentication & RBAC (Slice 1)

## Prerequisites

- Slice 0 complete (platform foundation)
- Local Postgres running (docker compose)
- `.env` configured

## Setup

```bash
# Apply Better Auth schema (generated by CLI)
cd spikes/auth-spike && npx @better-auth/cli generate --adapter drizzle -y
# Copy generated schema to packages/db/src/schema-auth.ts
# Apply RBAC migrations
npx drizzle-kit generate && npx drizzle-kit migrate
```

## Validate

```bash
# 1. Sign up
curl -s -X POST http://localhost:3000/api/auth/sign-up/email \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" -H "Origin: http://localhost:3000" \
  -d '{"email":"admin@example.com","password":"adminpass123","name":"Admin"}'
# Expected: 200 with user + token, Set-Cookie header

# 2. Sign in
curl -s -X POST http://localhost:3000/api/auth/sign-in/email \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" -H "Origin: http://localhost:3000" \
  -d '{"email":"admin@example.com","password":"adminpass123"}' -c cookies.txt
# Expected: 200 with user + token

# 3. Get session
curl -s http://localhost:3000/api/auth/get-session -b cookies.txt
# Expected: 200 with session + user (including displayName, isActive, isSuperAdmin)

# 4. Create API token (session auth)
curl -s -X POST http://localhost:3000/api/v1/tokens -b cookies.txt \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"name":"my-token","scopes":["content:read"]}'
# Expected: 201 with token (shown once)

# 5. Use API token (Bearer)
curl -s http://localhost:3000/api/v1/content-types -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>"
# Expected: 200 with content types (published only for public scope)

# 6. Permission check (deny)
# Attempt an action the user doesn't have permission for → 403
```

## Troubleshooting

- Sign-up returns 403 "Missing Origin": ensure Origin header is set.
- Session cookie not set: check CORS_ORIGINS and COOKIE_DOMAIN env vars.
- /ready returns 503: check DATABASE_URL and that migrations ran.
